# Native physical observation held-out plan, frozen before emitter inspection

The independent observer will use the unchanged Unit2C `chain_fixture` raw program to exercise the named complete destination paths. That fixture's original source SHA256 is 3f0e28a4f0cfa9ee34133d50db55d7e7df9ed18cb68629794dcd87139dcff9a4; exact extracted function hashes are in inherited-fixture-binding-v1.json. Native-only wrapper changes append an unused cycle where guarded coverage is needed; expected fuel remains the original independent schedule because the unused cycle never executes.

For each destination operation, the reviewer chooses payload poison 0xA5, preceding guard 0x96, and following guard 0x69. Poison all bytes in the actual declared positive destination extent immediately before the production write. Initialize both neighboring guard bytes before they are observed. For a frame-edge owner the observation-only module will extend the physical alloca with explicit outer guard bytes and rebase the owner arena pointer; the original owner offsets and complete operation text remain unchanged. No uninitialized bytes are loaded. Interleaved ordinary record slots in the chain provide safe neighbors for caller destinations; the one-owner callee requires the added outer guards.

Check complete zero payloads for [i32;0] (4 bytes), [bool;0]/[unit;0] (1 byte), and nonempty unit arrays (every byte). Do not inspect a full byte as a canonical bool guarantee for nonempty i1 payloads. Distinguishable logical i32/bool transfer checks remain separate. Observe ConstructArray Local/Temporary, MoveInitialize, Replace M/A, PrepareOwned staged destination, incoming owned parameter after allocation, ReturnOwned into caller result, and source-like self-replacement through a distinct temporary.

Retain the untouched production module, the instrumented observation module, and insertion records. Reconstruct/compare every original operation substring after stripping reviewer insertion chunks, so a successful observation cannot hide an edited operation. Instrumentation may add closed checking helpers but never replace operation behavior with a parallel array interpreter. It checks initialized physical byte storage only.

Narrow sensitivity controls use separate modules derived from the same untouched production IR. At the selected empty-i32 write, change only the full-width sentinel operation to a one-byte write/copy with LLVM-consistent load/store typing. Construction and each distinct emitted helper path (shared transfer, incoming, return if distinct) receive independent controls as needed. The observer must report the surviving poison bytes [0,165,165,165], or an equivalent explicit byte-check failure, and exit nonzero in actual source-free ELF. Empty bool/unit positive controls still pass. All mutant modules, commands, statuses, compiler/tool hashes and binary hashes remain retained; they are negative-control artifacts and never candidate code.

This establishes physical storage independently from reference zeroed arenas and source-visible scalar results. The exact textual insertion anchors will be selected only after candidate freeze; their semantic target and expected bytes are fixed here.
